allOf.description: This parameter must contain the merchant key that was provided by PayU while onboarding.

txnid.description: The transaction ID is a reference number for a specific order that is generated by the merchant. It is used to track the order and must be unique. PayU's system will not accept duplicate transaction IDs.

amount.description: This field should contain the payment amount for the transaction.

productinfo.description: This field should be a string containing a brief description of the product.

firstname.description: The first name of the customer.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phone.description: The phone number of the customer.

pg.description: This parameter must contain the payment mode code for debit card or credit card. For the simulation purposes, CC will be used.

bankcode.description: This parameter must contain the bankcode for debit card or credit card. For the simulation purposes, CC will be used.

pre_authorize.description: This parameter is set to 1 to pre-authorize payment.

ccnum.description: This parameter must contain the card number with which the amount will be pre-authorized.

ccname.description: This parameter must contain the name on card.

ccexpmon.description: This parameter must contain the card expiry month.

ccexpyr.description: This parameter must contain the card expiry year.

ccvv.description: This parameter must contain the card expiry CVV number that is present backside of the card.

allOf.description: The "surl" field is the success URL, which is the page PayU will redirect to if the transaction is successful. The merchant can handle the response at this URL after the customer is redirected there.
The "furl" field is the Failure URL, which is the page PayU will redirect to if the transaction is failed. The merchant can handle the response at this URL after the customer is redirected there.

hash.description: This parameter must contain the hash value to be calculated at merchant end.

lastname.description: Last name of the customer (must only contains alphabets).

curl.description: The "curl" field is the Cancel URL, which is the page PayU will redirect to if the transaction is canceled by the customer. The merchant can handle the response at this URL after the customer is redirected there.

udf1.description: User-defined fields (udf) are used to store any information corresponding to a particular transaction. You can use up to five udfs in the post designated as udf1, udf2, udf3, udf4, udf5.

udf2.description: User-defined fields (udf) are used to store any information corresponding to a particular transaction. You can use up to five udfs in the post designated as udf1, udf2, udf3, udf4, udf5.

udf3.description: User-defined fields (udf) are used to store any information corresponding to a particular transaction. You can use up to five udfs in the post designated as udf1, udf2, udf3, udf4, udf5.

udf5.description: User-defined fields (udf) are used to store any information corresponding to a particular transaction. You can use up to five udfs in the post designated as udf1, udf2, udf3, udf4, udf5.

key.title: key
key.description: The merchant key is a unique identifier for a merchant account in PayU's database. It is provided by PayU and use your Test key here.

bankcode.title: bankcode
bankcode.description: This parameter must contain the bankcode for debit card or credit card. For simulation, CC will be used.

furl.title: furl
furl.description: The "furl" field is the Failure URL, which is the page PayU will redirect to if the transaction is failed. The merchant can handle the response at this URL after the customer is redirected there.

pg.title: pg
pg.description: This parameter must contain the payment mode code for debit card or credit card. For simulation, CC will be used.

pre_authorize1.title: pre_authorize1
pre_authorize1.description: This parameter is set to 1 to pre-authorize payment using PayU Hosted Checkout.

surl.title: surl
surl.description: The "surl" field is the success URL, which is the page PayU will redirect to if the transaction is successful. The merchant can handle the response at this URL after the customer is redirected there.
